summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes obfuscated Bun payload on install
details: The package's preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`, declared in package.json) downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (bun-v1.3.13) into a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` bundled in the package. `math_init.js` is a ~728KB single-line, heavily obfuscated file tagged `// @bun @bun-cjs` with hex-named identifiers and a rotating string-array decoder (`WV8StW`/`n7gIxM`) — Bun-only bytecode-style content that cannot be inspected by Node-based tooling. setup.mjs additionally fingerprints the host (runs `ldd --version`, reads `/etc/os-release` to detect musl/Alpine, checks `process.platform` and `process.arch`) so the correct Bun variant is fetched across Linux glibc, Linux musl, macOS, and Windows on x64 and arm64. The advertised package purpose is a Vue radio-group input component, which has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime and execute an opaque 728KB payload under it at install time. The alternate-runtime approach specifically evades Node-only static analysis of the executed code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
